bug_locations: paginate: missing size validation (nonpositive sizes must raise ValueError)
paginate: cursor parsing/validation (unparseable, negative, or out-of-range cursors must raise ValueError)
paginate: next_cursor computation in the return statement (must be None at the end instead of always str(end))
explanation: Three interacting defects: (1) next_cursor was always str(end), so it never became None when the page reached the end of items; it is now None whenever end >= len(items). (2) There was no validation of size, so nonpositive sizes produced wrong slices instead of raising ValueError as specified. (3) There was no validation of the cursor: unparseable values leaked a raw int() error and, worse, negative cursor strings were silently accepted and used Python's negative indexing; the cursor is now parsed defensively and rejected with ValueError when it is not a valid zero-based index within bounds. The items are also materialized to a list so len() and slicing work for any iterable.
